answer: Directed response-window escrow: each identity must answer a randomized inbound query within a short window, and the reply is scored against a held-out reference before any payout. The gale of low-effort replies fails scoring, so an operator must staff each clone with genuine attention to keep it earning. Sustained scoring requires real session time, and the copper cost of that labor per identity per month exceeds what a clone can extract, making amplification unprofitable. A quill-level correction pass is also charged whenever scores dip, so margin erodes before scale is ever reached.
